questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: The antonym of the word protagonist is ________.
questions.explanationEn: A 'protagonist' is the leading or main character in a story or cause, whereas an 'antagonist' is the principal opponent or adversary. Thus 'antagonist' is the exact antonym.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
The figure shows two 4-tile patterns.
Either one or both of the patterns can be used any number of times and in any
orientation to construct a new pattern. Which one of the options below cannot be
constructed by using only these two 4-tile patterns assuming there are no overlaps
among them?
questions.explanationEn: Counting or matching the parity, color/shape adjacencies, and orientations of the two given 4-tile building blocks shows that Option (C) cannot be tiled without overlapping or altering the two 4-tile patterns (refer to the official figure).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a knock-out women’s badminton singles tournament where there are no
ties. The loser in each game is eliminated from the tournament. Every player
plays until she is defeated or remains the last undefeated player. The last
undefeated player is declared the winner of the tournament. If there are 64 players
in the beginning of the tournament, how many games should be played in total to
declare the winner of the tournament?
questions.explanationEn: In a single-elimination knock-out tournament with 64 players and no ties, each game eliminates exactly one player. To leave 1 undefeated winner, 64 - 1 = 63 players must be eliminated, requiring exactly 63 games.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A student needs to enroll for a minimum of 60 credits. A student cannot enroll for
more than 70 credits. The credits are divided amongst project and three distinct
sets of courses namely, core courses, specialization courses, and elective courses.
It is compulsory for a student to enroll for exactly 15 credits of core courses and
exactly 20 credits of project. In addition, a student has to enroll for a minimum of
10 credits of specialization courses. The maximum credits of elective courses that
a student can enroll for is ______
questions.explanationEn: The total credit cap is 70. Mandatory credits are 15 (core) + 20 (project) + at least 10 (specialization) = 45 credits minimum, leaving at most 70 - 45 = 25 credits for elective courses.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
‘When the teacher is in the room, all students stand silently.’
If the above statement is true, which one of the following statements is not
necessarily true?
optionsEn: If any student is not standing silently, then the teacher is not in the room.
When the teacher is in the room, all students are silent.
If all students are standing, then the teacher is in the room.
When the teacher is in the room, all students are standing.
questions.explanationEn: The given statement is T -> (S and Q) ('teacher in room -> all students stand silently'). Option (A) is its contrapositive, while (B) and (D) weaken the consequent. Option (C) asserts the converse (standing -> teacher in room), which does not necessarily follow.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Combinatorics deals with problems involving counting. For example, “How many
distinct arrangements of N distinct objects in M spaces on a circle are possible?”
is a typical problem in combinatorics. This kind of counting is sometimes used in
the modeling of several physical phenomena. Often, in such models, the different
combinatorial possibilities are assigned probability values. Assigning probabilities
enables the computation of the average values of physical quantities.
Consider the following statements:
P: Combinatorics is always invoked in the modeling of physical phenomena.
Q: Modeling some physical phenomena involves assigning probabilities to
combinatorial possibilities in order to compute average values of physical
quantities.
Based on the passage above, what can be inferred about statements P and Q?
optionsEn: P is False and Q is False
P is False and Q is True
P is True and Q is False
P is True and Q is True
questions.explanationEn: The passage says combinatorics is 'sometimes' used in modeling physical phenomena, making P ('always invoked') False. The passage explicitly states that assigning probabilities to combinatorial possibilities enables computing average values of physical quantities, making Q True.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
In the 2020 summer Olympics’ Javelin throw finals, Neeraj Chopra exhibited a
spectacular performance to win the gold medal. The silver medal was won by
Jakub Vadlejch and the bronze medal was won by Vitezlav Vesely. There were
six rounds of throws with each athlete having one throw per round. The best of
all the throws of each athlete is considered for the medal. Following were the
observations about the throws:
i.
The first and second rounds were dominated by Neeraj Chopra with a gold
medal performance in his second throw, while the other two athletes did
not have any medal winning throws in these rounds.
ii.
The throws in the last round by both Jakub Vadlejch and Vitezlav Vesely
were fouls and were not considered for scoring.
iii.
After four rounds, Vitezlav Vesely was in the second position and could
not improve upon his best throw in the succeeding rounds.
iv.
In the fourth round, the throw by Jakub Vadlejch was the best in that
round.
In which round did Vitezlav Vesely have his best throw?
questions.explanationEn: Vadlejch won silver (best overall after Chopra) and his best throw was not in rounds 1–2 (i) or round 6 (ii), while his round 4 throw was the best of round 4 (iv). Meanwhile, Vesely was 2nd after round 4 and never improved in rounds 5–6 (iii), and did not have a medal-winning throw in rounds 1–2 (i), so Vesely's best throw must have occurred in the Third round.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
An unbiased six-faced dice whose faces are marked with numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5,
and 6 is rolled twice in succession and the number on the top face is recorded
each time. The probability that the number appearing in the second roll is an
integer multiple of the number appearing in the first roll is __________
questions.explanationEn: Counting pairs (d1, d2) where d2 is an integer multiple of d1: for d1=1 (6 pairs: 1..6), d1=2 (3 pairs: 2,4,6), d1=3 (2 pairs: 3,6), d1=4 (1 pair: 4), d1=5 (1 pair: 5), d1=6 (1 pair: 6). Total favorable outcomes = 6 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 14 out of 36, giving probability 14/36 = 7/18.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
An urn contains one red ball and one blue ball. At each step, a ball is picked
uniformly at random from the urn, and this ball together with another ball of the
same color is put back in the urn. The probability that there are equal number of red
and blue balls after two steps is
questions.explanationEn: Initially the urn has 1 Red and 1 Blue ball. In step 1, whichever color is picked (probability 1/2 each), the urn ends up with 2 balls of that color and 1 of the other (3 balls total). To equalize the counts after step 2, step 2 must pick the minority color, which has probability 1/3 regardless of step 1, giving total probability 1/3.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider 4 × 4 matrices with their elements from {0, 1}. The number of such
matrices with even number of 1s in every row and every column is
questions.explanationEn: The top-left 3 x 3 entries in {0, 1} can be chosen freely in 2^9 = 512 ways. Each row's 4th entry and each column's 4th entry are then uniquely fixed to make the parity even (and the bottom-right entry automatically satisfies both row 4 and column 4 parity since total 1s in the 3x3 block fixes both), yielding 512 matrices.

questions.questionTextEn:
For n > 1, the maximum multiplicity of any eigenvalue of an n× n matrix with
elements from R is
questions.explanationEn: An n x n real matrix has a characteristic polynomial of degree n, so the algebraic (and geometric) multiplicity of any eigenvalue can be at most n. For example, the n x n identity matrix I_n has eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity n.

List I

1. Element of an array
Q. Indirect
2. Pointer

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a processor P whose instruction set architecture is the load-store
architecture. The instruction format is such that the first operand of any instruction
is the destination operand.
Which one of the following sequences of instructions corresponds to the high-level
language statement Z = X + Y ?
Note: X, Y, and Z are memory operands. R0, R1, and R2 are registers.
optionsEn: LOAD R0, X ADD Z, R0, Y
ADD R0, X, Y STORE Z, R0
LOAD R0, X LOAD R1, Y ADD R2, R0, R1 STORE Z, R2
questions.explanationEn: In a load-store architecture, ALU instructions operate only on registers while memory is accessed exclusively via LOAD and STORE instructions. Thus X and Y must first be loaded into R0 and R1, added into R2, and stored back to Z (Option D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Which one of the following dependencies among the register operands of different
instructions can cause a data hazard in a pipelined processor?
questions.explanationEn: A Read-After-Write (RAW, true dependency) hazard occurs when a later instruction needs a value written by an earlier instruction before it is ready in the pipeline. WAR and WAW are name (anti/output) dependencies in out-of-order execution, and Read-After-Read is never a hazard.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:

For all n> 1,
T1(n) = 4T1 (n

T2(n) = 5T2 (n
4) + Θ(log2 n)
Assume that for all n≤1, T1(n) = 1 and T2(n) = 1.
Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.explanationEn: For T2(n) = 5*T2(n/4) + Theta(log^2 n), n^(log_4 5) dominates log^2 n, so by Master Theorem Case 1, T2(n) = Theta(n^(log_4 5)) (~ n^1.161). Substituting into T1(n) = 4*T1(n/2) + T2(n), n^(log_2 4) = n^2 dominates n^(log_4 5), so again by Master Theorem Case 1, T1(n) = Theta(n^2).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
With respect to a TCP connection between a client and a server, which one of the
following statements is true?
optionsEn: The client and server use a two-way handshake mechanism before the start of data transmission
The server cannot initiate closing of the connection before the client initiates closing of the connection
The client and server can initiate closing of the connection at the same time
questions.explanationEn: TCP is full-duplex (C false), uses a three-way handshake (A false), and allows either endpoint to initiate teardown (B false). Both client and server can send FIN segments simultaneously (simultaneous close), so Option (D) is true.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following statements is/are true with respect to the interaction of a
web browser with a web server using HTTP 1.1?
optionsEn: HTTP 1.1 facilitates downloading multiple objects of the same webpage over the same TCP connection, if the objects are stored in the same server
HTTP 1.1 facilitates downloading multiple objects of the same webpage over the same TCP connection, even if they are stored in different servers
HTTP 1.1 facilitates sending a request for downloading one object without waiting for a previously requested object to be downloaded completely
HTTP 1.1 facilitates downloading multiple webpages on the same server to be downloaded over a single TCP connection
questions.explanationEn: HTTP/1.1 uses persistent TCP connections by default, allowing multiple objects of the same webpage (A) or multiple webpages on the same server (D) to reuse one TCP connection, and supports pipelining requests without waiting for earlier responses (C). A single TCP connection cannot span different origin servers (B false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let n > 1. Consider an n× n matrix M with its elements from R. Let the vector
(0, 1, 0, 0, ... , 0) ∈Rn be in the null space of M.
Which of the following options is/are always correct?
optionsEn: There are at least two non-zero vectors in the null space of M
questions.explanationEn: Because M has a non-zero vector v = (0, 1, 0, ..., 0) in its null space, M is singular, so det(M) = 0 (B). Since the null space is a vector subspace, every scalar multiple c*v (for all nonzero real c) is also in the null space, guaranteeing infinitely many (at least two) non-zero vectors (D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following Boolean expression of a function F :
F(P, Q) = (P̅ + Q) ⊕(P̅Q)
Which of the following expressions is/are equivalent to F ?
questions.explanationEn: Evaluating F(P, Q) = (P' + Q) XOR (P'Q): for (P,Q) = (0,0), 1 XOR 0 = 1; for (0,1), 1 XOR 1 = 0; for (1,0), 0 XOR 0 = 0; for (1,1), 1 XOR 0 = 1. This is the XNOR truth table, which equals (P XOR Q)' (A) and equivalently P' XOR Q (C).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the 8-bit signed integers X, Y and Z represented using the sign-magnitude
form. The binary representations of X and Y are as follows:
X: 10110100 Y: 01001100
Which of the following operations to compute Z result(s) in an arithmetic
overflow?
questions.explanationEn: In 8-bit sign-magnitude form, valid values span [-127, +127]. Here X = -0110100_2 = -52 and Y = +1001100_2 = +76. Computing Z = X - Y = -128 (B) and Z = -X + Y = +128 (C) both fall outside [-127, +127], causing arithmetic overflow, while X + Y = +24 and -X - Y = -24 fit in range.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let n be an odd number greater than 100. Consider a binary minheap with
n elements stored in an array P whose index starts from 1.
Which of the following indices of P do/does NOT correspond to any leaf node of
the minheap?
questions.explanationEn: In a 1-indexed binary heap of n elements, the internal (non-leaf) nodes are indices 1 through floor(n/2), and the leaves are floor(n/2) + 1 through n. Since n is odd, floor(n/2) = (n - 1)/2, so (n + 1)/2 and n are leaves while (n - 1)/2 (B) and (n - 3)/2 (C) are internal nodes (not leaves).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a hash table P[0, 1, ... , 10] that is initially empty. The hash table is
maintained using open addressing with linear probing. The hash function used is
h(x) = (x+ 7) mod 11.
Consider the following sequence of insertions performed on P:
1, 13, 22, 15, 11, 24
Which of the following positions in the hash table is/are empty after these insertions
are performed?
questions.explanationEn: Inserting with h(x) = (x + 7) mod 11 and linear probing: 1 -> 8, 13 -> 9, 22 -> 7, 15 -> 0, 11 -> 7 (occupied at 7,8,9 -> placed at 10), and 24 -> 9 (occupied at 9,10,0 -> placed at 1). Among {0, 10, 2, 1}, only position 2 remains empty.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following grammar where S is the start symbol, and a and b are
terminal symbols.
S →aSbS ∣ bS ∣ ε
Which of the following statements is/are true?
optionsEn: The string abb has two distinct derivations in this grammar
The string abab has only one rightmost derivation
The language generated by the grammar is undecidable
questions.explanationEn: Because S -> aSbS | bS | eps allows deriving 'b' via S -> bS -> b and also allows multiple parses when 'b' can be matched inside S or outside (e.g., 'abb' can be derived as a(b)bS -> abb or aS(bS) -> a(b)b -> ab? Specifically 'abb' has S -> aSbS -> abS -> abbS -> abb and S -> aSbS -> a(bS)bS -> abb, so A and B are true). For 'abab', the first 'a' must match the first 'b' via S -> aSbS and the second 'a' must match the second 'b', forcing a unique rightmost derivation (C).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let M be a nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) with 6 states over a finite
alphabet.
Which of the following options CANNOT be the number of states in the minimal
deterministic finite automaton (DFA) that is equivalent to M ?
questions.explanationEn: By subset construction, an NFA with 6 states has at most 2^6 = 64 subsets, so any equivalent minimal DFA can have at most 64 states. Therefore 65 (B) and 128 (D) states are impossible, while 32 and 1 are possible.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following C statements:
char *str1 = "Hello; /* Statement S1 */
char *str2 = "Hello;"; /* Statement S2 */
int *str3 = "Hello"; /* Statement S3 */
Which of the following options is/are correct?
optionsEn: S1 and S2 have syntactic errors
S2 has a lexical error and S3 has a syntactic error
S1 has a lexical error and S3 has a semantic error
S1 has a syntactic error and S3 has a semantic error
questions.explanationEn: In S1, the string literal "Hello; lacks a closing double quote, causing an unterminated string token (lexical error). In S3, assigning a char* string literal "Hello" to an int* variable causes a type mismatch (semantic error). S2 is valid C.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements is/are true?
optionsEn: For a grammar to be LL(1), it must be left-recursive
For a grammar to be LL(1), it must be left-factored
The LL(1) parsers are more powerful than the SLR parsers
questions.explanationEn: An LL(1) grammar must be free of left recursion and must be left-factored so that FIRST sets of alternative productions for the same non-terminal are disjoint (C). LL(1) is predictive without backtracking (A false), cannot be left-recursive (B false), and is strictly less powerful than SLR(1)/LR(1) on grammars (D false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
With respect to deadlocks in an operating system, which of the following
statements is/are FALSE?
optionsEn: Banker’s algorithm is used to prevent deadlocks
Deadlock formation can be prevented by ensuring that the hold and wait condition is not allowed
An assignment edge in a resource allocation graph is marked from a process to a resource
A safe state guarantees that all processes can finish without formation of a deadlock
questions.explanationEn: Banker's algorithm is used for deadlock AVOIDANCE rather than deadlock prevention (so A is FALSE). In a resource allocation graph, an assignment edge points from a resource to the process holding it (process-to-resource is a request edge, so C is FALSE). Statements B and D are true.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let P, Q, R and S be the attributes of a relation in a relational schema. Let X ⟶Y
indicate functional dependency in the context of a relational database, where
X, Y ⊆{P, Q, R, S}.
Which of the following options is/are always true?
questions.explanationEn: If P -> R and Q -> S, then by augmentation and union (Armstrong's axioms), PQ -> RS holds (C). If P -> R, then by augmentation PQ -> R holds (D). Options (A) and (B) are invalid FD inferences (e.g., if P -> R holds, Q need not determine R).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
In the context of relational database normalization, which of the following
statements is/are true?
optionsEn: It is always possible to obtain a dependency-preserving 3NF decomposition of a relation
It is always possible to obtain a dependency-preserving 1NF decomposition of a relation
It is not always possible to obtain a dependency-preserving BCNF decomposition of a relation
It is not always possible to obtain a dependency-preserving 2NF decomposition of a relation
questions.explanationEn: A dependency-preserving 3NF decomposition always exists via Bernstein's synthesis algorithm (A), and every relation with atomic domains is already in 1NF (B). However, BCNF decompositions cannot always preserve all functional dependencies (C; e.g., R(A,B,C) with AB -> C, C -> B), whereas 2NF decompositions can always be made dependency-preserving (D false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
The height of a binary tree is the number of edges in the longest path from the root
to a leaf in the tree. The maximum possible height of a full binary tree with
23 nodes is _________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: In a full binary tree (every internal node has 2 children) with n = 23 nodes, total internal nodes = (23 - 1)/2 = 11. Maximum height is achieved by a skewed full tree where each level adds 1 internal node and 1 leaf, giving height equal to the number of internal nodes = 11 edges.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a system consisting of k instances of a resource R, being shared by
5 processes. Assume that each process requires a maximum of two instances of
resource R and a process can request or release only one instance at a time. Further,
a process can request the second instance of the resource only after acquiring the
first instance.
The minimum value of k for the system to be deadlock-free is ________. (answer
in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Each of the 5 processes needs at most 2 instances of R. Deadlock occurs if every process holds 1 instance and waits for 1 more (5 instances). With k = 5 + 1 = 6 instances, by the pigeonhole principle at least one process can obtain its 2nd instance, finish, and release both, guaranteeing deadlock freedom.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the real valued variables X, Y and Z represented using the IEEE 754 single-
precision floating-point format. The binary representations of X and Y in hexadecimal
notation are as follows:
X: 35C00000 Y: 34A00000
Let Z = X+ Y.
Which one of the following is the binary representation of Z, in hexadecimal
notation?
questions.explanationEn: Decoding IEEE 754 single precision: X = 0x35C00000 has biased exp 107 (2^(-20)) and significand 1.5, so X = 1.5 * 2^(-20). Y = 0x34A00000 has biased exp 105 (2^(-22)) and significand 1.25, so Y = 1.25 * 2^(-22) = 0.3125 * 2^(-20). Adding gives Z = 1.8125 * 2^(-20) = 1.1101_2 * 2^(-20), which encodes as 0x35E80000.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
The size of the physical address space of a processor is 232 bytes. The capacity of a
cache memory unit is 223 bytes. The cache block size is 128 bytes. The cache
memory unit can be built as a direct mapped cache or as a K-way set-associative
cache, where K= 2L and L∈{1, 2, 3}. Let the length of the TAG field be M bits
for the direct mapped cache, and N bits for the set-associative cache.
Which one of the following options is true?
questions.explanationEn: The cache size (2^23 bytes) and block size (128 = 2^7 bytes) are fixed, giving 2^16 total blocks. In direct-mapped cache, all 16 bits form the index, so M = 32 - 16 - 7 = 9 tag bits. In K-way set-associative cache (K = 2^L), the number of sets drops by a factor of 2^L, reducing index bits by L and increasing tag bits by L, so N = M + L.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let P be the set of all integers from 1 to 15. Consider any order of insertion of the
elements of P into a binary search tree that creates a complete binary tree.
Which one of the following elements can NEVER be the third element that is
inserted?
questions.explanationEn: A complete binary search tree on {1..15} is a perfect binary tree of height 3, so its root must be the median 8, and its root's left and right children must be 4 and 12 (the medians of 1..7 and 9..15). The third inserted element can be 12 (if 4 was 2nd), or a child of 4 (2 or 6) or a child of 12 (10 or 14) if inserted after 4 or 12, but 5 is at depth 3 (child of 6) and cannot be inserted as the 3rd element.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let G(V, E) be an undirected, edge-weighted graph with integer weights. The weight
of a path is the sum of the weights of the edges in that path. The length of a path is
the number of edges in that path.
Let s∈V be a vertex in G. For every u∈V and for every k ≥0, let dk(u) denote
the weight of a shortest path (in terms of weight) from s to u of length at most k. If
there is no path from s to u of length at most k, then dk(u) = ∞.
Consider the statements:
S1:
For every k ≥0 and u ∈V, dk+1(u) ≤dk(u).
S2:
For every (u, v) ∈E, if (u, v) is part of a shortest path (in terms of
weight) from s to v, then for every k≥ 0, dk(u) ≤dk(v).
Which one of the following options is correct?
optionsEn: Both S1 and S2 are true
Neither S1 nor S2 is true
questions.explanationEn: Every path of length at most k is also a path of length at most k + 1, so the minimum weight over the larger set cannot exceed the previous minimum, making S1 true. However, edge weights can be negative, so along a shortest path from s to v using (u, v) with w(u, v) < 0, we can have dk(u) > dk(v), making S2 false.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a relational database schema with two relations R(P, Q) and S(X, Y).
Let E = {⟨u⟩∣∃v ∃w ⟨u, v⟩∈R ∧ ⟨v, w⟩ ∈S} be a tuple relational calculus
expression.
Which one of the following relational algebraic expressions is equivalent to E ?
questions.explanationEn: In E = {<u> | exists v, exists w (<u, v> in R and <v, w> in S)}, the second attribute of R (R.Q) equals the first attribute of S (S.X), and the first attribute of R (R.P) is projected out. Joining S and R on S.X = R.Q and projecting P yields Option (B).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
A TCP sender successfully establishes a connection with a TCP receiver and starts
the transmission of segments. The TCP congestion control mechanism’s slow-start
threshold is set to 10000 segments. Assume that the round-trip time is fixed at
1 millisecond. Assume that the sender always has data to send, the segments are
numbered from 1, and no segment is lost. Let t denote the time (in milliseconds) at
which the transmission of segment number 2000 starts.
Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.explanationEn: During TCP slow start (ssthresh = 10000), the sender transmits 2^k segments in round k (at t = k ms): 1 segment in round 0 (t=0), 2 in round 1 (t=1), ..., cumulatively 2^(k+1) - 1 segments through round k. After round 9 (t = 9 ms), 2^10 - 1 = 1023 segments have been sent, and segment 2000 falls in round 10 (1024 to 2047), so transmission starts at 10 <= t < 11 ms.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the implementation of sliding window protocol over a lossless link, with a
window size of W frames, where each frame is of size 1000 bits (including header).
The bandwidth of the link is 100 kbps (1k = 103) and the one-way propagation delay
is 100 milliseconds. Assume that processing times at the sender and receiver are zero
and the transmission time of acknowledgements is also zero. Which one of the
following options gives the minimum size of W (in number of frames) required to
achieve 100% link utilization?
questions.explanationEn: Transmission time per frame T_t = 1000 bits / 100 kbps = 10 ms, and one-way propagation delay T_p = 100 ms (RTT = 200 ms). For 100% link utilization, W >= 1 + 2*(T_p / T_t) = 1 + 2*(100 / 10) = 21 frames.

Which of the following statements is/are true?
optionsEn: f′ is not differentiable over R
questions.explanationEn: For x >= 0, |x|/2 - x = -x/2 and x - |x|/2 = x/2, so f(x) = -x^2 / 4. For x < 0, |x|/2 - x = -3x/2 and x - |x|/2 = 3x/2, so f(x) = -9x^2 / 4. Thus f(x) <= 0 everywhere with global/local maximum 0 at x = 0 (A, no local minimum so B false); f'(x) = -x/2 (x >= 0) and -9x/2 (x < 0) matches 0 at x = 0 so f' is continuous over R (C), but its left and right slopes at 0 are -9/2 != -1/2 so f' is not differentiable at 0 (D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let G(V, E) be a simple, undirected graph. A vertex cover of G is a subset
V′ ⊆V such that for every (u, v) ∈E, u∈V′or v∈V′. Let the size of the smallest
vertex cover in G be k. Let S be any vertex cover of size k.
For a vertex v∈V, which of the following constraints will always ensure that
v∈S ?
optionsEn: The degree of v is at least k+ 1
The vertex v is on a path of length k+ 1
The vertex v is on a cycle of length k+ 1
The vertex v is a part of a clique of size k
questions.explanationEn: If deg(v) >= k + 1 and v were NOT in S, then S would have to include all >= k + 1 neighbors of v to cover its incident edges, contradicting |S| = k; hence deg(v) >= k + 1 guarantees v in S (A). Being on a path/cycle of length k+1 or a clique of size k does not force v into every minimum vertex cover (e.g., K_k has a cover of size k-1).

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a Boolean function F with the following minterm expression:
F(P, Q, R, S) = ∑m (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 10, 12, 13, 14)
Which of the following options is/are the minimal sum-of-products expression(s)
of F ?
questions.explanationEn: Plotting the 10 minterms {1,2,3,4,5,7,10,12,13,14} on a 4-variable K-map gives essential prime implicants P'S (covering 1,3,5,7) and QR' (covering 4,5,12,13). The remaining minterms 2, 10, 14 are minimally covered by either {P'Q'R, PRS'} (Option B) or {PQS', Q'RS'} (Option D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let G(V, E) be a simple, undirected, edge-weighted graph with unique edge weights.
Which of the following statements about the minimum spanning trees (MST)
of G is/are true?
optionsEn: In every cycle C of G, the edge with the largest weight in C is not in any MST
In every cycle C of G, the edge with the smallest weight in C is in every MST
For every vertex v ∈V, the edge with the largest weight incident on v is not in any MST
For every vertex v ∈V, the edge with the smallest weight incident on v is in every MST
questions.explanationEn: By the cycle property of MSTs with distinct weights, the heaviest edge in any cycle C can never belong to the MST (A). By the cut property applied to the cut ({v}, V\{v}), the lightest edge incident on any vertex v must belong to every MST (D). Counterexamples exist for (B) (lightest edge of a cycle may not be in MST if lighter paths exist) and (C).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following pseudocode for depth-first search (DFS) algorithm which
takes a directed graph G(V, E) as input, where d[v] and f[v] are the discovery time
and finishing time, respectively, of the vertex v ∈V.
DFS(G):
unmark all v∈V
t ←0
for each v∈V
if v is unmarked
t←Explore(G, v, t)
end if
end for
Explore(G, v, t):
mark v
t ←t+ 1
d[v] ←t
for each (v, w) ∈E
if w is unmarked
t←Explore(G, w, t)
end if
end for
t ←t + 1
f[v] ←t
return t
Suppose that the input directed graph G(V, E) is a directed acyclic graph (DAG).
For an edge (u, v) ∈E, which of the following options will NEVER be correct?
questions.explanationEn: In a DAG, there are no back edges, so for any edge (u, v) we can have a tree/forward edge where u discovers and finishes around v (d[u] < d[v] < f[v] < f[u], A) or a cross edge where v is completely finished before u is discovered (d[v] < f[v] < d[u] < f[u], C). Option (B) corresponds to a back edge (impossible in a DAG), and Option (D) violates the parenthesis theorem of DFS timestamps.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let L1 and L2 be two languages over a finite alphabet, such that L1 ∩L2 and L2 are
regular languages.
Which of the following statements is/are always true?
questions.explanationEn: Every regular language is context-free, so L2 being regular guarantees L2 is context-free (C). L1 itself can be any arbitrary non-regular or even undecidable language (for example, if L2 = empty set, L1 intersect L2 = empty set is regular regardless of L1), making A, B, and D false in general.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following context-free grammar G.
S→abaABAbba
A→aaBBAb | bBabaa
B→aBb | ab
In the above grammar, S is the start symbol, a and b are terminal symbols, and A and
B are non-terminal symbols.
Let L(G) be the language generated by the grammar G. For a string s∈L(G), let
n1(s) be the number of a’s in s and n2(s) be the number of b’s in s.
Which of the following statements is/are true?
optionsEn: There is a string s∈L(G) such that n1(s) < n2(s)
There is a string s∈L(G) such that n1(s) > 2n2(s)
questions.explanationEn: In B -> aBb | ab, every step adds 1 'a' and 1 'b' (n_a = n_b). Accounting for the terminals in S -> abaABAbba and A -> aaBBAb | bBabaa, every derived string satisfies n1(s) >= n2(s) (B) and n1(s) <= 2*n2(s) (D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a system that has a cache memory unit and a memory management unit
(MMU). The address input to the cache memory is a physical address. The MMU
has a translation lookaside buffer (TLB). Assume that when a page is evicted from
the main memory, the corresponding blocks in the cache are marked as invalid.
For a given memory reference, which of the following sequences of events can
NEVER happen?
optionsEn: TLB miss, Page table hit, Cache hit
TLB hit, Page table miss, Cache hit
TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache hit
TLB miss, Page table miss, Cache miss
questions.explanationEn: A TLB caches page-table translations for pages present in main memory, and evicting a page invalidates its TLB/cache entries. Thus if a page table miss occurs (page fault, page not in main memory), neither a TLB hit (B) nor a physical-address cache hit (C) is possible.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
An undirected, unweighted, simple graph G(V, E) is said to be 2-colorable if there
exists a function c: V→{0, 1} such that for every (u, v) ∈E, c(u) ≠c(v).
Which of the following statements about 2-colorable graphs is/are true?
optionsEn: If G is 2-colorable, then G may contain cycles of odd length
If G is 2-colorable, then G may contain cycles of even length
An optimal algorithm for testing whether G is 2-colorable runs in time Θ(|V| + |E|), if G is represented as an adjacency list
An optimal algorithm for testing whether G is 2-colorable runs in time Θ(|E| log|V|), if G is represented as an adjacency list
questions.explanationEn: A graph is 2-colorable if and only if it is bipartite, which is equivalent to containing NO odd-length cycles (so it may contain even cycles, B, while A is false). Bipartiteness is tested via BFS/DFS 2-coloring in Theta(|V| + |E|) time using adjacency lists (C).

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
An ISP having an address block 202.16.0.0/15 assigns a block of 6000 IP addresses
to a client, using the classless internet domain routing (CIDR) super-netting
approach. Which of the following address blocks can be assigned by the ISP?
questions.explanationEn: To assign at least 6000 IP addresses using CIDR, we need 2^13 = 8192 addresses, corresponding to a /19 prefix (32 - 13 = 19). A valid /19 block inside 202.16.0.0/15 must have its 3rd octet divisible by 2^5 = 32 (i.e., 0, 32, 64, 96, ...). Thus 202.16.0.0/19 (A), 202.17.64.0/19 (B), and 202.16.32.0/19 (C) are valid, while 202.17.24.0/19 (24 not divisible by 32) is invalid.

questions.pyqTag: GATE Computer Science (CS) • 2026 Set 1 Official Paper
questions.questionTextEn:
Let G be an undirected graph, which is a path on 8 vertices. The number of matchings
in G is ______. (answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Let M(n) be the number of matchings (including the empty matching) in a path P_n on n vertices. Either vertex n is unmatched (M(n-1) ways) or matched with vertex n-1 (M(n-2) ways), giving the Fibonacci recurrence M(n) = M(n-1) + M(n-2) with M(1) = 1, M(2) = 2: M(3)=3, M(4)=5, M(5)=8, M(6)=13, M(7)=21, and M(8)=34.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a hard disk with a rotational speed of 15000 rpm. The time to move the
read/write head from a track to its adjacent track is 1 millisecond. Initially, the head
is on track 0. The number of sectors per track is 400. The sector size is 1024 bytes.
It is necessary to transfer data from 10 randomly located sectors in each of the
following tracks in the order: 5, 12 and 7.
The total time for the data transfer (in milliseconds) from the hard disk is _________.
(rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: At 15000 rpm (250 rps), 1 rotation = 4 ms, average rotational latency = 2 ms, and 1-sector transfer time = 4/400 = 0.01 ms. Head movement across tracks 0 -> 5 -> 12 -> 7 takes 5 + 7 + 5 = 17 ms. Reading 30 random sectors (10 per track) takes 30 * (2 + 0.01) = 60.3 ms, for a total of 17 + 60.3 = 77.3 ms.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider a relational database schema with a relation R(A, B, C, D). If {A, B} and
{A, C} are the only two candidate keys of the relation R, then the number of superkeys
of relation R is ______. (answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The candidate keys are AB and AC. Using inclusion-exclusion on subsets of {A, B, C, D}: superkeys containing AB = 2^2 = 4, superkeys containing AC = 2^2 = 4, and superkeys containing ABC = 2^1 = 2. Total superkeys = 4 + 4 - 2 = 6.
